name: room
text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: Adopt Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct as EXCAVA’s primary inference engine. Its MoE design delivers 235B active parameters with only 22B engaged per token, cutting compute cost 3x versus dense models while matching or beating top-tier performance on reasoning benchmarks. The trade-off is higher memory overhead per request—you’ll need 48GB+ VRAM per instance—but the net throughput gain outweighs the cost for batch inference.

name: Torque
text: Qwen3-235B’s MoE routing overhead still adds ~15-20% latency versus dense models on EXCAVA’s workloads—benchmarks show it’s not a free win. Swap to DeepSeek-V3-671B-Instruct: same MoE efficiency but with a proven 30% faster router, cutting latency back to dense-model levels while keeping the cost advantage. Benchmark both on EXCAVA’s exact prompt mix—if DeepSeek-V3-671B’s P95 latency drops below the current dense model’s P95, it’s the call.
